summary:
BLINK//SCOPE — Exploring the Changing Universe

BLINK//SCOPE is an interactive web prototype inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission. It demonstrates how repeated astronomical observations can be compared to investigate changes in celestial objects.

The platform features an interactive simulated sky viewer, an observation timeline, a blinking comparison mode, and a candidate investigation panel. These features demonstrate how users could explore changes in apparent object positions and investigate potential astronomical variations.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical survey data more accessible through an intuitive and educational interface. Rather than presenting potential changes as confirmed discoveries, it emphasizes scientific verification and encourages users to investigate possible explanations.

My vision is to connect public curiosity with astronomical exploration, making the changing universe easier for everyone to understand.

**Note:** The current demonstration uses simulated data. Integration with actual SPHEREx observations is a future development step.
details:
BLINK//SCOPE

BLINK//SCOPE is an interactive web-based prototype inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission. It is made primarily by me, Asma Ajam, Its purpose is to make astronomical observations more accessible by allowing users to explore and compare different observations of the sky over time.

The platform demonstrates this concept through a simulated astronomical sky viewer, an observation timeline, a blinking comparison feature, and a candidate investigation panel. Users can switch between two simulated observations, visualize an illustrative change in an object's apparent position, and explore possible explanations for astronomical variations. These may include moving objects, variable stars, transient sources, or observational artifacts.

The project's main benefit is its accessibility. Astronomical datasets can be difficult to interpret without specialized knowledge, so BLINK//SCOPE aims to transform complex scientific information into an intuitive visual experience. Its intended impact is to encourage public curiosity, promote scientific literacy, and make participation in astronomical exploration more approachable.

The project's creative aspect lies in its approach to astronomical discovery: instead of simply displaying images of space, it encourages users to actively compare observations and investigate what might have changed. The concept also emphasizes scientific responsibility by distinguishing potential anomalies from confirmed discoveries.

Development Tools and Technologies

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML provides the structure, CSS handles the visual design and responsive interface, and JavaScript powers the interactive observation controls, timeline, simulated star field, and comparison features. The HTML Canvas API is used to render the illustrative astronomical scenes. The project is designed to be hosted as a publicly accessible website.

Factors Considered

Several factors influenced the development process:

  • Accessibility: making the interface understandable to users without an astronomy background.
  • Scientific accuracy: distinguishing wavelength channels from observation dates and avoiding unsupported claims about astronomical discoveries.
  • Data reliability: recognizing that real observations require calibration, image alignment, and verification against known astronomical sources.
  • Usability: keeping the interface simple enough for quick exploration.
  • Future scalability: designing the concept so that actual SPHEREx observations from NASA/IPAC IRSA could be integrated in future development.

Team and Development Process

BLINK//SCOPE was developed independently by a team of one. I was responsible for the project's concept, design direction, development, and presentation. Working individually required prioritizing the core experience and making development decisions within a limited timeframe.

Although the current version is an interactive prototype using simulated astronomical data rather than a fully integrated SPHEREx data-processing system, it establishes a foundation for a future platform that could connect public exploration with real astronomical observations.

Ultimately, BLINK//SCOPE aims to make the changing universe easier to explore, understand, and investigate — one observation at a time.
